title: Three things the game does that Rust had to copy before the numbers agreed
notes: Isolde's icicle is timed by two clocks. The game holds her second cast (the Shatter) back with the page's clock and opens it with the round's clock. The two round differently, so at the last frame the hold lets go a hair early about one time in three, and she casts a Shatter that hits nothing and stands still for half a second. It depends on how long the page has been open, so the real game itself is a little different from page to page. Worth fixing in the game one day; Rust copies it as it is.

The opponent flickers. When the opponent has been pushed, the game shows it at the pushed spot, but on every frame it walks it is at the unpushed spot until the next frame. Whoever looks at it in between (the player's hero, its hits, bolts) sees the unpushed one. It is a few centimetres to a few tens of centimetres, enough to change who is in reach.

The computer players remember the last fight. Which way each one strafes, and for how long yet, is not reset when a new fight starts, and the player's side starts the very first fight strafing the other way than the opponent.
